I run a university. Im also an Uber driver.

Part time uber drivers are just doing it for extra income on top of a full time job whereas for regular cab drivers it's not just for beer money it's their livelihoods. Uber keep fares low because they want as many customers as possible but take a massive chunk of income from their drivers which means if uber gets rid of regular cab drivers then it can drive down prices even more resulting in too many drivers chasing fewer jobs and this means drivers will be on poverty wages. Once this level is achieved the standard of drivers will also drop (cabs are regulated for reasons) there will be less drivers willing to cover slow shifts (Monday to Thursday) and graveyard shifts leaving people with less services than regulated cabs.

One other very important point is insurance, a woman was killed by an uber driver but uber denied that he was an employee stating that he was contracted therefore uber was not liable.

If you get into a regular cab you know you are insured, you know the driver is vetted, you know the car is Road worthy (has to pass a government check for certification once a year) None of which uber does.

I know these things because I am an ex taxi driver.
